CFML Language Reference: Functions

ArrayAppend

Appends a value to the end of an array, making the array one element longer. The value can be anything: a string, a number, a date, or even another array or structure.

Category

Array functions

Syntax

ArrayAppend(array, value)

Parameters

array
The array to change. The array is changed in place.
value
The value to add as the new last element.

Returns

TRUE (prints as YES) when the element was added.

Usage

Because the function changes the array you pass and only returns TRUE, the 1999 idiom is <CFSET Temp = ArrayAppend(MyArray, "value")>. To add an element at the front, use ArrayPrepend; to add one in the middle, use ArrayInsertAt.

Appending an array to a one-dimensional array is how you build a two-dimensional array row by row.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<!--- Build a shopping list one item at a time --->
<CFSET Groceries = ArrayNew(1)>
<CFSET Temp = ArrayAppend(Groceries, "Coffee")>
<CFSET Temp = ArrayAppend(Groceries, "Bagels")>
<CFSET Temp = ArrayAppend(Groceries, "Floppy disks")>

<CFOUTPUT>
<P>The list now has #ArrayLen(Groceries)# items:</P>
<OL>
<CFLOOP INDEX="i" FROM="1" TO="#ArrayLen(Groceries)#">
  <LI>#Groceries[i]#
</CFLOOP>
</OL>
</CFOUTPUT>

See also

ArrayPrepend, ArrayInsertAt, ArrayLen, ArrayNew
